answer: A sybil operator would have to wander across many machines, paying full energy per identity, while honest agents register once. One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is a proof-of-work registration gate tied to a unique hardware root: each agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle whose seed is derived from a physical attestation, making each identity cost real compute and a distinct device. Like a marble dropped into a zephyr, cheap accounts get swept away by rising puzzle difficulty as the network grows. This model fits agent sa0030's threat model.
